title: Max's Kansas City: Art, Glamour, Rock and Roll

description.main: A photographic history of the New York club Max's Kansas City, edited by Steven Kasher.
description.extended:
A picture history of Max's Kansas City, the Park Avenue South restaurant and club where artists, poets, Warhol's circle and rock musicians shared tables from 1965 into the early 1980s.

Edited by Steven Kasher, the book collects photographs of the celebrities and musicians who passed through, with essays on the club's history. Contributions come from Lou Reed, Lenny Kaye, Danny Fields, Lorraine O'Grady and Steven Watson. It was published in conjunction with a 2010 exhibition at Steven Kasher Gallery in New York.

Mickey Ruskin opened the club at 213 Park Avenue South in 1965, and it became a gathering place for artists of the Park Place and Green galleries, Warhol and his entourage, the Velvet Underground and the glam rock scene around David Bowie, Iggy Pop and the New York Dolls. The original site closed in December 1981.
